Two bank variants agree on driver/data boundary. Per-song schema unresolved; generic Data only. See sound-data-review.json and BC42/BA57 decoded driver.

regions.summary: Bank-local sound tables and command streams, selected by the five-channel driver. Split low/high start tables at CPU $8027/$8063 and restart tables at $809F/$80DB use 5*track+channel. Preset pointers at $8117/$814C select four APU bytes. Timed events are [value, delay_minus_one]; FE selects a preset, FF restarts, FC/FB stop and E2 stores an argument minus one. Individual song identities and stream boundaries are unresolved; this combined payload remains generic Data.

Quantize direction from that position to the scene reference and store it with category one. Publish the list bound and queue the wave palette. Exact game identities of the waves remain unresolved.

Clamp the next wave row to a table limit, increment the wave/state byte, and use its high nibble as the actor type. Fill three thirteen-byte actors with distinct random position selectors 0..3, tracking used selectors in a bit mask. Initialize fractions, state, timer, flags and parameter; set each position from paired X offsets and wave-row*8 plus paired Y offsets. Quantize direction from that position to the scene reference and store it with category one. Publish the list bound and queue the wave palette. Exact game identities of the waves remain unresolved.

units.summary: Preserve caller Y and sample a signed coordinate offset selected by actor category and direction. Convert the resulting actor pixel position to tile coordinates, wrapping X to nine bits, and query the fixed tile classifier. Retain the maximum class, then invoke this bank's $802A hook with A=1. Carry set from the hook ends sampling; otherwise the count initialized to one is decremented, with another offset plane selected if the hook extended it. Restore Y and return carry set exactly when the maximum class exceeds the actor category. Hook-specific scene effects remain described at that bank's hook.

regions.summary: First call the current bank API $801E to transform A into an adjustment. Actor flag bit 7 with state nibble zero or seven suppresses the subtraction. Otherwise subtract when the adjustment is strictly below the current meter value. Recompute its scaled four-unit group, store a six-frame feedback counter and request effect 5. An adjustment reaching the meter sets scene-status high nibble $50, clears four scene contact gates, stores $80 at $05E9 and requests effect 7. This is probably a damage/depletion path; exact bank-dependent scaling and game identity remain unresolved.

units.name: Scene meter subtraction and depletion
units.summary: First call the current bank API $801E to transform A into an adjustment. Actor flag bit 7 with state nibble zero or seven suppresses the subtraction. Otherwise subtract when the adjustment is strictly below the current meter value. Recompute its scaled four-unit group, store a six-frame feedback counter and request effect 5. An adjustment reaching the meter sets scene-status high nibble $50, clears four scene contact gates, stores $80 at $05E9 and requests effect 7. This is probably a damage/depletion path; exact bank-dependent scaling and game identity remain unresolved.

Otherwise subtract when the adjustment is strictly below the current meter value. Recompute its scaled four-unit group, store a six-frame feedback counter and request effect 5. An adjustment reaching the meter sets scene-status high nibble $50, clears four scene contact gates, stores $80 at $05E9 and requests effect 7. This is probably a damage/depletion path; exact bank-dependent scaling and game identity remain unresolved.

regions.summary: Sum the first byte of each selected composite descriptor as the requested sprite count. At most 61 sprites fit after the three reserved OAM entries. If over budget, compute a contiguous cyclic interval of descriptor sprites to omit, carrying its endpoints across frames when the total changes only slightly. Larger changes rephase from the NMI frame counter low five bits. $FF endpoints disable omission when within budget. Counts are bytes; this code assumes bounded descriptor totals.

If an origin coordinate is negative, set it to zero and shift the target by the same amount, preserving the relative vector. Compute absolute X/Y differences and a quadrant-table offset, then divide the larger difference by the low byte of (smaller>>4). A zero low-byte divisor uses ratio $FF. All point scratch is destructive. Valid game coordinate ranges are assumed; this is a quantizer, not full-precision atan2.

If an origin coordinate is negative, set it to zero and shift the target by the same amount, preserving the relative vector. Compute absolute X/Y differences and a quadrant-table offset, then divide the larger difference by the low byte of (smaller>>4). A zero low-byte divisor uses ratio $FF. Compare the byte quotient against descending thresholds $90/$33/$1D/$13; reflect the threshold index when Y is dominant and combine it with the quadrant offset to read a 12-direction result from $DAD0. All point scratch is destructive. Valid game coordinate ranges are assumed; this is a quantizer, not full-precision atan2.

If an origin coordinate is negative, set it to zero and shift the target by the same amount, preserving the relative vector. Compute absolute X/Y differences and a quadrant-table offset, then divide the larger difference by the low byte of (smaller>>4). A zero low-byte divisor uses ratio $FF. Compare the byte quotient against descending thresholds $90/$33/$1D/$13; reflect the threshold index when Y is dominant and combine it with the quadrant offset to read a 12-direction result from $DAD0. All point scratch is destructive. Valid game coordinate ranges are assumed; this is a quantizer, not full-precision atan2.

State-five actors enter state nine, save max(current timer,fifteen) in the extension byte and use timer fifteen. Success returns carry clear; the equality rejection also returns the comparison carry.

Preserve that full-byte behavior rather than describing a simple bit toggle.

regions.summary: Scene-dependent tile classification. Preserve X, query the background tile at tile coordinates $BA/$BB, and classify the returned tile ID. A scene with a non-$FF first threshold returns 0/1/2 according to two thresholds. Otherwise read a scene-dependent lookup table through base $1A/$1B. Mode zero adds phase[$93]&$3F to the high byte; mode two uses the base directly; other modes combine phase parity and actor state with offset tables. In that last path, four LSRs of actor state replace the carry from the low-pointer addition before the high-byte ADC. Preserve this exact carry behavior; it is not an ordinary 16-bit pointer addition. The meanings of the returned classes remain unresolved.

regions.summary: Scene-record view bounds and clipping. X points to a five-byte scene record. Its byte 2 selects a descriptor using type*4+state_low2. A negative descriptor skips extent lookup; otherwise a pointer-table entry supplies four extent bytes. Compare record row and low-six-bit column with view origins, admitting a small offscreen margin. Carry set means fully rejected. Carry clear returns a mask: bit 0 marks vertical clipping and bit 1 horizontal clipping. Also update first/last record offsets once the vertical test passes. Descriptor values and the exact object meanings remain unresolved.

A negative descriptor skips extent lookup; otherwise a pointer-table entry supplies four extent bytes. Compare record row and low-six-bit column with view origins, admitting a small offscreen margin. Carry set means fully rejected. Carry clear returns a mask: bit 0 marks vertical clipping and bit 1 horizontal clipping. Also update first/last record offsets once the vertical test passes. Descriptor values and the exact object meanings remain unresolved.

A negative descriptor skips extent lookup; otherwise a pointer-table entry supplies four extent bytes. Compare record row and low-six-bit column with view origins, admitting a small offscreen margin. Carry set means fully rejected. Carry clear returns a mask: bit 0 marks vertical clipping and bit 1 horizontal clipping. Also update first/last record offsets once the vertical test passes. Descriptor values and the exact object meanings remain unresolved.

A negative descriptor skips extent lookup; otherwise a pointer-table entry supplies four extent bytes. Compare record row and low-six-bit column with view origins, admitting a small offscreen margin. Carry set means fully rejected. Carry clear returns a mask: bit 0 marks vertical clipping and bit 1 horizontal clipping. Also update first/last record offsets once the vertical test passes. Descriptor values and the exact object meanings remain unresolved.

regions.summary: Background patch descriptor and vertical clipping. Select the record type/state descriptor through $12/$13. A negative descriptor sets the cache bit and skips rendering. Otherwise resolve its pointer through $14/$15 and draw a rectangular background patch. Format: signed/byte column and row offsets, tile width, tile height, width*height tile bytes, then a two-byte attribute header and packed two-bit palette fields. The first attribute-header byte is the source row stride in quadrant fields; the second is not read by this routine. Clip vertically to the 30-row view, queue visible tile rows, merge palette fields into attribute RAM, then queue only the touched attribute rows. Caller supplies valid dimensions, source data and queue/mapper context. Width and height must be positive; zero dimensions would underflow the countdown loops.

Otherwise resolve its pointer through $14/$15 and draw a rectangular background patch. Format: signed/byte column and row offsets, tile width, tile height, width*height tile bytes, then a two-byte attribute header and packed two-bit palette fields. The first attribute-header byte is the source row stride in quadrant fields; the second is not read by this routine. Clip vertically to the 30-row view, queue visible tile rows, merge palette fields into attribute RAM, then queue only the touched attribute rows. Caller supplies valid dimensions, source data and queue/mapper context. Width and height must be positive; zero dimensions would underflow the countdown loops.

regions.summary: Downward scroll and row exposure. Preserve A and advance the vertical scroll shadow by the unsigned step in $BD, wrapping modulo 240. On a tile-row crossing, prepare one new row at logical_row+30 and its attributes before advancing the logical row. The scene-specific row bound at $C619 prevents advancing past the map end; clamp the step to the last pixel of the current tile row there. Update the 16-bit vertical pixel origin by the actual step. The interface handles one newly exposed row per call, so callers must use small steps.

At logical row zero clamp the step to the current within-tile scroll offset. Subtract the actual step from the 16-bit vertical pixel origin. One newly exposed row is prepared per call.

regions.summary: Rightward bounded or wrapping scroll. Preserve A and add the horizontal step at $BC. Mode bit $04 allows wrapping across nametables: toggle PPUCTRL bit 0 on byte overflow. Otherwise clamp at scroll $FF using the remaining pixels in the current tile. Advance the horizontal pixel-origin word modulo 512 using the actual step. Horizontal movement here changes scroll state only; it does not build a new tile-column payload.

Wait until the previous alternate NMI transfer finishes (flag bit 7 clear), compute $2000+32*destination_row and expand 64 tile bytes into the staging buffer. Keep the logical row in scratch for the attribute pass.

regions.summary: Scrolled attribute staging and publication. regions.summary: Typed object allocation and capacity budgets. A selects a two-byte type descriptor via $D4/$D5. Its low nibble is a capacity weight; the next byte initializes the object mode. Enforce separate normal-type weight and reserved-byte budgets, using the fixed table of multiples of 11. Types with low-seven-bit index below $18 establish a weight limit (double weights 1..3, otherwise the weight itself); other types share the remaining 14-slot budget. On success append an 11-byte record at $0700+end, copy the two coordinate words from $B4..$B7, initialize common fields and return carry clear. Carry set means capacity rejection. No separate bounds check protects the byte-sized end cursor; callers must keep budget state valid.

The updater may remove/compact a record: carry set retries at the same byte offset. For retained records, a nonnegative mode calls $D07A then $F07D; a negative mode calls $D153. These outgoing render/action helpers remain separate review dependencies. The compacting loop requires valid aligned list state.

Test the working point against category-indexed rectangles around actor coordinate words. On contact, parameter high nibble $20/$30 selects actor states 5/6 and sets its timer to $50; other values call $D880 with the contact parameter. Set the object contact mode and return carry set. List bounds must fit the 13-byte byte-index stride.

Type descriptors are five bytes: packed category/exclusion code, X offset, width, Y offset, height. Scale record tile coordinates by eight, add offsets and test the object working point against the resulting rectangle. Contact either updates record state/timer or subtracts a byte-sized value, then selects an object contact mode. Carry set reports contact; carry clear means no eligible record contained the point.

Require category equality between object type bit 7 and the type descriptor high nibble. Type descriptors are five bytes: packed category/exclusion code, X offset, width, Y offset, height. Scale record tile coordinates by eight, add offsets and test the object working point against the resulting rectangle. Contact either updates record state/timer or subtracts a byte-sized value, then selects an object contact mode. Carry set reports contact; carry clear means no eligible record contained the point.

phase1.evidence: Static fixed-last-bank control flow from accepted engine code. MMC3 $E000-$FFFF always physical bank31; call continuations stay physically resolved despite unknown switch windows. Indirect successors remain unresolved. See fixed-closure.json; natural use not asserted.

regions.summary: Object movement script control commands. Byte-7 low nibble is a direction index; byte 8 selects a movement script (zero means direct motion) through the pointer table at $16/$17. Byte 10 is the script cursor. Ordinary bytes adjust direction relative to the current index with one modulo-12 correction, then move. Commands $80..$83 control repeat/end, cursor jump, script replacement and object cloning. Commands can continue decoding in the same call; scripts must terminate their command chains. Exact script assignments are bank-local.

Commands $80..$83 control repeat/end, cursor jump, script replacement and object cloning. Commands can continue decoding in the same call; scripts must terminate their command chains. Exact script assignments are bank-local.

Add each byte increment to its six-bit fractional accumulator in record bytes 4/5, retain low six bits and pass the upper two bits as unsigned X/Y movement magnitudes. These are byte additions: overflow past 255 is discarded. Finally dispatch one of 12 direction handlers through split tables at $F1CA/$F1D6. The handlers apply signed combinations to the coordinate words.

regions.summary: Three-byte state scrambler. Update the three-byte state at $21..$23 and return state[$21] XOR state[$22]. Shift the old $21 right twice, rotate its bit 1 through $23 then $22, subtract old $21 using the outgoing $22 carry, then shift/rotate the subtraction result back into $21. Shift the old $21 right twice, rotate its bit 1 through $23 then $22, subtract old $21 using the outgoing $22 carry, then shift/rotate the subtraction result back into $21. This looks like a pseudorandom scrambler; its period and statistical properties are not established.

regions.summary: NMI scene CHR animation dispatch. Run from NMI only while the scene active bit is set. With scene bit $40 clear, frame phase 5 modulo 16 selects the scene-specific animation; otherwise frame phase 1 modulo 8 updates the shared CHR registers. Actor flags can suppress the scene-specific update. These writes select MMC3 CHR registers, not PRG physical bank indices. Table contents and the graphics represented remain partly unresolved.

For bands with more than eight sprites, rotate the removal start using a persistent phase and hide excess sprites until only eight remain. This distributes sprite omissions across frames. Visible input Y values must produce band indices below 30; the routine does not clamp the index.

regions.summary: Palette fade to base. Compare all 32 displayed colors with their base values. For each difference, use the base low nibble when the displayed value is $0F; otherwise add $10. After a changed pass, wait four frames, queue both palette halves and drain the queue; repeat until exact equality. This assumes palette values arranged so these discrete steps can reach the base. Arbitrary mismatched low nibbles would not converge.

regions.summary: Uniform $FF payload bounded by byte transitions. Prior reference and neighboring-code inspection supports generic non-code data; no specific consumer or record layout is established. Do not infer unused storage solely from repetition.

phase1.evidence: Four zero bytes followed by ASCII DRAGONSTRIKE! and compact non-instruction trailer fields; bounded by previous accepted code and validated vector data. No natural selector coverage asserted.

regions.summary: Trailer metadata between the fixed-bank code/fill and validated interrupt vectors: four zero bytes, an ASCII signature and compact following fields. Exact metadata purpose remains unresolved; it is preserved as Data, not decoded as instructions.

units.name: BoundedDataPayload262128

phase1.evidence: Three little-endian 6502 vectors in fixed final PRG bank; reset independently matches startup PC.
phase1.label: InterruptVectors

regions.summary: Little-endian CPU vectors in fixed bank 31: NMI, reset and IRQ respectively. Physical pointer words are distinct from the CPU execution addresses they contain.

phase1.evidence: Validated iNES declares 256 KiB CHR ROM. NES 2-bit planar 8x8 tile backing, bank selected by MMC3; separate non-CPU storage.
phase1.label: CHRPatternPlanes

regions.summary: CHR ROM: 32 physical 8 KiB banks of NES two-plane pattern tiles (16 bytes per 8x8 tile). These are PPU pattern data, not CPU instructions. Tile-to-object and scene assignments remain unresolved; keep the full payload local.
